sampling_model.design: Observational two-cohort panel with adoption at date \(3\) for \(D=1\) and no adoption for \(D=0\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent and identically distributed complete five-date panels \(O_i\).
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort membership fixes the realized treatment path; no anticipation holds through date \(2\).
sampling_model.overlap: Both cohorts have positive probability and both latent types have positive mass within each cohort.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is fitted; empirical frequencies on the fixed \(120\)-cell support face feed the guarded analytic recovery map.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 14 uniquely identifies the finite latent-type Markov parameter under Assumptions RSM, M, and ID from a sufficiently long short panel.
Theorem 1 identifies initial distributions, transition kernels, and type probabilities up to a common permutation from four consecutive observations under Assumptions 1--3.
The paper estimates latent conditional moments by simultaneous diagonalization followed by weighted empirical averages and derives regular asymptotics for the estimated weights.
Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration bounds hold for maxima with arbitrary covariance matrices when marginal variances are positive.
The efficient influence function is obtained by projecting a pathwise derivative onto the model tangent space.

body.tldr: Four matched active-state slices identify two latent Markov components even when a common absorbing state makes the usual all-state terminal factor singular. Spectral projectors remove eigenvector scaling, full terminal row sums recover exit probabilities, a pseudoinverse transports the second active predecessor factor, and the observable absence of date-‑\(1\) exit exhausts each type mass. The resulting analytic cell-probability map identifies type-specific and aggregate first-post state ATTs over the full compatible fiber, yields a saturated finite-multinomial canonical gradient, and supports guarded Gaussian-multiplier bands uniformly over a compact margin class despite singular ATT correlation. An exact rational witness verifies the map, an outside-face pair shows why initial absorbers break conditional type recovery, and constrained-Markov efficiency remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Short-panel latent Markov reconstruction uses nonsingular terminal factors and positive transition arrays, while causal transition-independence work inherits those conditions; a common absorbing observed state creates identical terminal rows and structural zeros, and existing pointwise likelihood inference does not cover a data-dependent guarded recovery map on that face.
project_justification.niche: Two active states and one absorbing exit state still leave four invertible active minors whose cycle product carries type signatures, while stochastic row sums and no initial absorption contain normalization information absent from a survival-conditioned reduction.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an explicit projector, row-sum, and pseudoinverse recovery formula with a full-fiber uniqueness theorem, exact boundary evidence, an analytic saturated-model gradient, and uniform multiplier coverage under observable buffered margins.

body.related_work: Ahn and Kasahara (2026), Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, provide the closest causal setup and four-slice inverse-cancellation argument, but Assumption ID requires nonsingular terminal factors and strictly positive transitions that exclude a common absorbing row; their writing arc from incoherent categorical trends to transition-based counterfactuals is retained here. Higgins and Jochmans (2023), Theorem 1 and Sections 2--3, establish constructive Markov-mixture recovery and common label alignment; their full-rank factor logic informs the proof, while the present target uses active minors and stochastic row sums on an excluded support face and is not claimed to subsume their theorem. Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016) reconstruct homogeneous Markov mixtures under a state-count restriction that does not cover two types with only two active states. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017) supply the closest estimator template: differentiate a simultaneous-diagonalization construction and propagate estimated weights into conditional moments. Deaner and Ku (2026) show why absorption calls for transition or hazard restrictions, but address binary aggregate duration effects rather than multi-state latent-type recovery. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, 2015) provide multiplier and anti-concentration tools under arbitrary correlation; the new task is their integration with guard-uniform linearization of the spectral map. Newey (1990) supplies the projection geometry for the open constrained-efficiency question. Rao and Risch (2026) are the interpretation consumer because their linked firm panel separates entry and exit adjustments and could distinguish offsetting exit effects across latent productivity types.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance \(\Sigma(p)\) is the efficiency bound only for the specified off-model continuation \(\Phi\) in the saturated multinomial support-stratum model. It is not asserted to be efficient in the smaller compatible Markov model, which can use common kernels and date \(4\). The initial-absorption pair proves failure of type-mass and conditional-type-effect identification, not failure of aggregate ATT identification. The exact multiplier quantile is the mathematical object; a fixed finite number of Monte Carlo draws requires an additional approximation analysis.
body.honest_scope: The proposal proves sufficient recovery on a declared regular absorbing face, not a necessary-and-sufficient identification frontier. In the special case of no exit transitions, all exit ATT coordinates reduce to zero and the active-state formulas collapse to ordinary two-state latent Markov recovery; with one latent type, the projector step disappears and the ATT reduces to the transition-independence plug-in. The unresolved content is constrained-model efficiency, while weak eigengaps, unknown type count, initial-absorption sharp bounds, and approximate common transitions remain separate angles.
